SOURCE = HamiltonianPath
Hamiltonian Path (undirected, any endpoints).

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...]}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

returns to its start, using only edges of the graph.

Edge cases: graphs with n <= 2 are always no (a simple graph needs at

Now I understand the problem. Let me analyze the classic reduction and its edge cases.

The standard reduction: given graph G with n vertices, add a new vertex x connected to all vertices of G. Then G has a Hamiltonian path iff G' has a Hamiltonian cycle. But this fails for n=1 (G' would have 2 vertices, no cycle, while source is yes). Let me verify all edge cases and implement.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Hamiltonian Path to Hamiltonian Cycle.

Reduction
---------
Given a Hamiltonian Path instance G = (V, E) with |V| = n, build a
Hamiltonian Cycle instance G' by adding one brand-new vertex x and
connecting it to every vertex of G:

    V' = V u {x},   E' = E u { {v, x} : v in V }.

Correctness for n >= 2
----------------------
